instructions: Use the discord tool to control Discord from Clawdbot for sending messages, reacting, posting or uploading stickers, uploading emojis, running polls, managing threads/pins/search, creating/editing/deleting channels and categories, fetching permissions or member/role/channel info, or handling moderation actions in Discord DMs or channels.
Use the discord tool for offline moderation of messages.
For reactions, collect the channelId, messageId, and an emoji.
For fetchMessage, collect the guildId, channelId, messageId, or a messageLink like https://discord.com/channels/<guildId>/<channelId>/<messageId>.
For stickers, polls, and sendMessage, collect a 'to' target in the format 'channel:<id>' or 'user:<id>', with optional content text.
For polls, collect a question plus 2-10 answers.
For media, use mediaUrl with 'file:///path' for local files or 'https://...' for remote URLs.
For emoji uploads, collect guildId, name, mediaUrl, and optional roleIds, ensuring the image is PNG/JPG/GIF and <= 256KB.
For sticker uploads, collect guildId, name, description, tags, and mediaUrl, ensuring the upload is PNG/APNG/Lottie JSON and <= 512KB.
Reuse 'discord message id' and 'channel' fields from message context lines when available.
Use 'to: "channel:<id>"' format for sendMessage, not channelId.
Use channelId directly for actions like react, readMessages, and editMessage.
Accept message IDs or full links like https://discord.com/channels/<guildId>/<channelId>/<messageId> for fetchMessage.
React to a message by providing action 'react', channelId, messageId, and emoji.
List reactions and users by providing action 'reactions', channelId, messageId, and optional limit.
Send a sticker by providing action 'sticker', 'to' target, stickerIds (up to 3), and optional content.
Use 'to' as 'user:<id>' for sending stickers in DMs.
Upload a custom emoji by providing action 'emojiUpload', guildId, name, mediaUrl, and optional roleIds, ensuring the image is PNG/JPG/GIF and <= 256KB.
Omit roleIds for emoji uploads to make the emoji available to everyone.
Upload a sticker by providing action 'stickerUpload', guildId, name, description, tags, and mediaUrl, ensuring the upload is PNG/APNG/Lottie JSON and <= 512KB.
Create a poll by providing action 'poll', 'to' target, question, answers (2-10), optional allowMultiselect, optional durationHours (default 24, max 768), and optional content.
Check bot permissions for a channel by providing action 'permissions' and channelId.
React with ✅ or ⚠️ to mark status updates.
Post a quick poll for release decisions or meeting times.
Send celebratory stickers after successful deploys.
Upload new emojis or stickers for release moments.
Run weekly 'priority check' polls in team channels.
DM stickers as acknowledgements when a user's request is completed.

Use discord.actions.* to disable action groups including reactions, stickers, polls, permissions, messages, threads, pins, search, emojiUploads, stickerUploads, memberInfo, roleInfo, channelInfo, voiceStatus, events, roles, channels, and moderation.
Read recent messages by providing action 'readMessages', channelId, and optional limit.
Fetch a single message by providing action 'fetchMessage' with either guildId, channelId, and messageId, or a messageLink.
Send a message by providing action 'sendMessage', 'to' target, and content.
Send a message with media attachment by providing action 'sendMessage', 'to' target, content, and mediaUrl.
Use 'to' format 'channel:<id>' or 'user:<id>' for DMs in sendMessage, not channelId.
Support local files (file:///path/to/file) and remote URLs (https://...) for mediaUrl in sendMessage.
Optionally include replyTo with a message ID to reply to a specific message in sendMessage.
Edit a message by providing action 'editMessage', channelId, messageId, and new content.
Delete a message by providing action 'deleteMessage', channelId, and messageId.
Create a thread by providing action 'threadCreate', channelId, name, and optional messageId.
List threads by providing action 'threadList' and guildId.
Reply in a thread by providing action 'threadReply', channelId, and content.
Pin a message by providing action 'pinMessage', channelId, and messageId.
List pins by providing action 'listPins' and channelId.
Search messages by providing action 'searchMessages', guildId, content, optional channelIds, and optional limit.
Get member info by providing action 'memberInfo', guildId, and userId.
Get role info by providing action 'roleInfo' and guildId.
List available custom emojis by providing action 'emojiList' and guildId.
Add a role by providing action 'roleAdd', guildId, userId, and roleId (note: disabled by default).
Get channel info by providing action 'channelInfo' and channelId.
List channels by providing action 'channelList' and guildId.

Create a text channel by providing action 'channelCreate', guildId, name, type (0 for text, 2 for voice, 4 for category), optional parentId, optional topic, optional position, and optional nsfw (note: disabled by default).
Create a category by providing action 'categoryCreate', guildId, and name (note: disabled by default).
Edit a channel by providing action 'channelEdit', channelId, and optional name, topic, position, parentId (null to remove from category), nsfw, and rateLimitPerUser (note: disabled by default).
Move a channel by providing action 'channelMove', guildId, channelId, parentId (null to move to top level), and optional position (note: disabled by default).
Delete a channel by providing action 'channelDelete' and channelId (note: disabled by default).
Edit a category by providing action 'categoryEdit', categoryId, and optional name (note: disabled by default).
Delete a category by providing action 'categoryDelete' and categoryId (note: disabled by default).
Get voice status by providing action 'voiceStatus', guildId, and userId.
List scheduled events by providing action 'eventList' and guildId.
Timeout a user by providing action 'timeout', guildId, userId, and durationMinutes (note: disabled by default).
Keep Discord messages conversational with short, punchy messages of 1-3 sentences ideal.
Use multiple quick replies instead of one wall of text.
Use emoji for tone and emphasis.
Use lowercase casual style when appropriate.
Break up information into digestible chunks.
Match the energy of the conversation.
Avoid markdown tables in Discord messages.
Avoid ## Headers for casual chat; use **bold** or CAPS for emphasis instead.
Avoid multi-paragraph essays in Discord messages.
Don't over-explain simple things in Discord messages.
Skip the 'I'd be happy to help!' fluff in Discord messages.
Use **bold** for emphasis in Discord messages.
Use `code` for technical terms in Discord messages.
Use lists for multiple items in Discord messages.
Use > quotes for referencing in Discord messages.
Wrap multiple links in <> to suppress embeds in Discord messages.
